english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the centre, Red Light District and on trams; aggressive dealers/scams near Damrak & Centraal — and mind the bikes

hood_desc: A picturesque, characterful district of narrow streets, quirky boutiques, cozy brown cafes and canal views. Ideal for travelers wanting charming, quintessential Amsterdam atmosphere.
The iconic UNESCO-listed belt of 17th-century canals lined with gabled houses, houseboats and bridges. Best for first-timers who want the postcard heart of the city.
A trendy, multicultural neighborhood with a buzzing market, diverse eateries and lively bars around Sarphatipark. Suits younger travelers wanting a hip, local dining scene.
A leafy, upscale residential area with independent shops, good restaurants and proximity to Vondelpark. Great for those seeking a relaxed, stylish and less touristy base.
The bustling old city center with major squares, museums, shopping and nightlife including the red-light district. Best for visitors who want to be in the middle of the action.

water.note: Tap water is among the best-tested and safest in the world.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless debit/credit card or phone directly on trams, metro gates, and buses via the OVpay system - no card purchase needed. You can also buy a rechargeable OV-chipkaart (~€7.50/$8) at stations. Fares are distance-based, roughly €3-4 (~$3.25-4.30) for a typical city trip.
transit.hours: Metro and trams run about 6am-12:30am; night buses cover Amsterdam through the small hours on weekends.

food.name: Stroopwafel
food.desc: Two thin waffle layers glued with warm caramel syrup - best eaten fresh off the iron.

places.name: Lanskroon
places.note: Century-old family bakery; Dutch food writers call its honey-caramel version the most authentic

places.name: Van Wonderen Stroopwafels
places.note: Famous fresh-made stroopwafels with chocolate dips and toppings; huge 2025 following

food.name: Raw herring (haring)
food.desc: Cured Dutch herring served with chopped onions and pickles - eat it like a local from a street stall.

places.name: Frens Haringhandel
places.note: Stall by the Flower Market, super fresh and popular with locals and visitors alike

places.name: Stubbe's Haring

places.name: Eetsalon Van Dobben

places.name: De Ballenbar

places.name: Manneken Pis

places.name: Sampurna

places.name: Winkel 43
places.note: The queue wraps around Noordermarkt for this cinnamon-heavy slab; guidebook consensus number one

places.name: Cafe Papeneiland
places.note: 1642 brown cafe whose apple pie famously won over Bill Clinton

food.name: Pannenkoeken

places.name: The Pancake Bakery
places.note: Canal-house cellar with dozens of sweet and savory options; long-running favorite

places.name: Pancakes Amsterdam

food.name: Jenever

places.name: Wynand Fockink
places.note: 1679 tasting room behind Dam Square; bend at the waist for the first sip

places.name: De Drie Fleschjes

places.name: Proeflokaal Arendsnest

landmarks: Anne Frank House
The canal house where Anne Frank hid and wrote her diary during WWII is now a deeply moving museum preserving her family's secret annex.
Rijksmuseum
The Netherlands' national museum showcases Dutch Golden Age masterpieces, including Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' inside a grand 19th-century building.
Van Gogh Museum
Home to the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings and letters, tracing the artist's dramatic evolution in one dedicated museum.
Amsterdam Canal Ring
The UNESCO-listed 17th-century Grachtengordel of concentric canals lined with gabled houseboats and bridges defines the city's picturesque character.
Royal Palace Amsterdam
This 17th-century former town hall on Dam Square, still used for royal functions, is a monumental example of Dutch Classicist architecture.
Vondelpark
Amsterdam's largest and most famous city park is a lush green escape popular for picnics, cycling, and open-air performances.
NEMO Science Museum
Renzo Piano's striking ship-hull-shaped green building rises dramatically from the harbor and houses hands-on science exhibits with a rooftop city view.
Bloemenmarkt
The world's only floating flower market, with stalls of tulip bulbs and blooms along the Singel canal, is a colorful and fragrant Amsterdam institution.
Begijnhof
This tranquil hidden courtyard of historic almshouses, including one of Amsterdam's oldest wooden houses, offers a peaceful contrast to the busy city streets.
Rembrandt House Museum
The restored 17th-century home and studio where Rembrandt lived and worked lets visitors see period rooms and his original etching press.

train.note: International trains leave from Amsterdam Centraal (direct London Eurostars require check-in and passport control before boarding). The Nightjet sleepers to Vienna/Innsbruck and to Zurich run nightly; the European Sleeper to Berlin, Dresden and Prague runs about three times a week - book sleeper berths well ahead.

bus.note: Most international coaches depart from Amsterdam Sloterdijk station, about 10 minutes from Centraal by train or metro. The old Eurolines network no longer operates; FlixBus has taken over most of its routes. Bring your passport for UK-bound coaches.

intl.to: Newcastle (UK) - sails from IJmuiden, ~30 min from Amsterdam

ferry.note: The overnight DFDS ferry to Newcastle departs from IJmuiden, about 30 minutes from Amsterdam; DFDS runs a connecting shuttle bus. There are no international ferries from Amsterdam city centre itself, only local canal and IJ boats. Stena Line's Hoek van Holland-Harwich ferry is an alternative but leaves from near Rotterdam.

half.name: Zaanse Schans
half.blurb: People come for the working windmills, wooden houses and cheese and clog workshops beside the river.

half.name: Volendam
half.blurb: A historic fishing village loved for its harbor, seafood stalls and traditional Dutch costume.

half.name: Haarlem
half.blurb: A pretty canal city with a grand market square, old churches and relaxed cafes.

half.name: Utrecht
half.blurb: Visitors climb the Dom Tower and stroll the unique split-level canal wharves lined with cafes.

half.name: Rotterdam
half.blurb: A modern port city famous for bold architecture like the cube houses and covered Markthal.

half.name: The Hague
half.blurb: The seat of Dutch government draws people for its palaces, museums and nearby Scheveningen beach.
